attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The missing Yang-Mills estimate is the no-boundary-sector theorem: after bulk Wilson renormalization, reflected Wilson collars must have \(B_{ij}=e^{i\alpha_i-i\alpha_j}\) and hence \(K=0\) for all finite mixed OS pairings. We do not yet have a nonperturbative bound excluding a connected coincident-footprint boundary OPE for Wilson hairpins.
steps: Start with the fixed-collar cone argument: for each \(\delta>0\), regulated reflection positivity gives \(N^{(a,L,\delta)}\ge0\). Because the RG topology is assumed valid for reflected collar probes, entrywise convergence passes positivity to \(N^{(\delta)}\), and the collar limit gives \(N\ge0\).

Use the earlier trace analysis: local mirror-flat composites pass to the reflection plane by distributional continuity, and positive additive boundary contacts vanish once diagonal trace continuity is known. Therefore the unresolved Wilson obstruction can be isolated as a multiplicative matrix \(B\) with \(N=B\circ M\).

Ask what is required to infer the intended target positivity \(M\ge0\) from the proved collar positivity \(N\ge0\). For a bridge lemma that is independent of accidental properties of one finite family, this requires the reciprocal entrywise multiplier \(B^{[-1]}\) to preserve positivity, hence to be a positive Schur multiplier on every finite OS matrix.

Assume the boundary anomaly is not arbitrary but comes from a genuine positive boundary sector: \(B_{ij}=\langle\eta_i,\eta_j\rangle\), \(B_{ii}=1\). Then every two-by-two minor of \(B^{[-1]}\) gives \(1-|B_{ij}|^{-2}\ge0\), while Cauchy-Schwarz gives \(|B_{ij}|\le1\). Hence \(|B_{ij}|=1\), so equality in Cauchy-Schwarz forces \(\eta_i\) and \(\eta_j\) to be collinear for all pairs.

Conclude that a valid same-theory bridge permits only a one-dimensional boundary sector, equivalently a diagonal phase/congruence already included in the locked renormalization convention. Any normalized damping \(|B_{ij}|<1\) is not a harmless Wilson-loop normalization; it is evidence that the collar construction proves positivity for an enlarged bulk-plus-boundary theory.

Linearize this conclusion around smooth Wilson hairpins. A nonzero connected boundary covariance \(C_\partial\) yields \(|B_{\xi\eta}|<1\) for distinguishable boundary jets, hence violates the reciprocal-Schur condition. Therefore the analytic target becomes \(C_\partial=0\) or, equivalently, vanishing of all logarithmic cross-ratios \(K\) on the dense Wilson core.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The finite-dimensional Schur/Gram rigidity argument is valid, but it is conditional. It assumes the boundary defect has been isolated multiplicatively and, more importantly, it does not prove the analytic statement \(C_\partial=0\) for four-dimensional Yang-Mills Wilson loops. A concrete proof must control cusp/hairpin renormalization at the reflection plane without changing the test algebra.

assumptions: For every fixed \(\delta>0\), \(N^{(a,L,\delta)}_{ij}=S_{a,L}(\Theta T_\delta F_i,T_\delta F_j)\) is positive semidefinite by regulated reflection positivity.
The RG/cutoff-removal topology is valid for reflected collar probes: \(N^{(a,L,\delta)}\to N^{(\delta)}\), and then \(N^{(\delta)}\to N\) entrywise for each finite family.
Diagonal trace continuity and positivity have already removed positive additive boundary contacts, so the remaining possible defect is multiplicative: \(N_{ij}=B_{ij}M_{ij}\), with \(B_{ij}\ne0\).

The Wilson boundary defect, if present, is representable as a normalized Gram kernel \(B_{ij}=\langle \eta_i,\eta_j\rangle_{\mathcal K_\partial}\), \(B_{ii}=1\), for boundary hairpin states \(\eta_i\). This is the natural case for a positive boundary sector produced by a collar collapse.
definitions: source object: regulated reflection-positive Schwinger forms \(S_{a,L}\) on a locked gauge-invariant positive-time algebra \(\mathcal A_W^+\), with Wilson/local observables moved off the reflection plane by collar embeddings \(T_\delta\).

target object: continuum OS-positive Schwinger functions \(S\) on the same locked gauge-invariant observable algebra, with OS matrices \(M_{ij}=S(\Theta F_i,F_j)\) for finite positive-time families \(F_i\).

controlled interface: regulated reflection-positive Schwinger forms -> OS-positive continuum Schwinger functions, controlled by convergence of every finite reflected collar quadratic form and by the absence of nontrivial boundary hairpin factors.

same-theory condition: the collar limit may apply predeclared bulk Wilson renormalizations and harmless diagonal congruences, but it may not adjoin a new boundary Hilbert factor, boundary counterterm, pair-dependent cusp factor, or changed Wilson-loop algebra.

equations.label: collar-limit factorization
equations.valid_when: Valid when all additive contact terms vanish and the residual Wilson boundary anomaly is multiplicative after the fixed bulk renormalization scheme has been locked.

equations.label: reciprocal-Schur transfer condition
equations.latex: M=B^{[-1]}\circ N,\qquad B^{[-1]}_{ij}=1/B_{ij};\quad N\ge0\ \forall N\ \Longrightarrow\ M\ge0\ \forall N\ \text{ only if }\ B^{[-1]}\ge0.
equations.valid_when: Valid as a universal finite-matrix bridge condition by the Schur product theorem; without positivity of the reciprocal kernel, collar positivity does not formally imply target OS positivity.

equations.label: normalized-Gram rigidity
equations.valid_when: Valid for every two-by-two principal minor. Combined with Cauchy-Schwarz for the Gram kernel, it forces all boundary states to be collinear; normalized phases are only diagonal congruences.

equations.label: two-state damping falsifier
equations.latex: B=\begin{pmatrix}1&\beta\\\overline\beta&1\end{pmatrix},\quad 0<|\beta|<1,\quad N=\begin{pmatrix}1&r\\\overline r&1\end{pmatrix},\quad |\beta|<|r|\le1\ \Longrightarrow\ M=B^{[-1]}\circ N\ \text{ has }\det M=1-|r/\beta|^2<0.
equations.valid_when: Valid as a finite-dimensional falsifier of any bridge that tries to infer same-theory positivity from collar positivity while allowing a nonrank-one normalized boundary damping factor.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Find two locked Wilson hairpin observables whose normalized reflected collar anomaly has \(|B_{12}|<1\), or compute a nonzero logarithmic cross-ratio \(K\). Either is a falsifier of the same-theory bridge unless a separate restriction on the actual \(N\)-matrices avoids the reciprocal-Schur counterexample.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This lemma converts the remaining Wilson obstruction into a Hilbert-sector rigidity statement. It proves that the formal closed-cone step is insufficient unless the reflected Wilson boundary collapse produces no genuine boundary degrees of freedom.
candidate_lemmas.statement: No-boundary-sector Schur rigidity lemma: after fixed-collar RG convergence has produced a positive collar-limit OS matrix \(N\), the intended same-theory OS matrix \(M\) is protected from a Wilson boundary anomaly \(B\) only when the boundary anomaly is a rank-one diagonal congruence. Equivalently, if \(N=B\circ M\) and \(B\) is a normalized Gram kernel of possible reflected Wilson hairpin boundary states, then the closed-cone argument is a valid same-theory positivity bridge for all finite families only if the boundary Hilbert sector is one-dimensional. A nontrivial boundary state overlap \(|B_{12}|<1\) is a finite-matrix falsifier of the bridge unless an independent Yang-Mills estimate proves that the actual collar matrices never probe the dangerous reciprocal Schur multiplier.

assumptions: The boundary anomaly is smooth to second order along the chosen Wilson-core hairpin variations.
Bulk perimeter/cusp renormalizations have already been fixed away from the reflection plane.
The local mirror-flat composite sector has trace continuity, so the only remaining singular contribution is the Wilson hairpin boundary OPE.
The boundary covariance is positive semidefinite as a Gram covariance of the candidate boundary sector.
definitions: \(\xi\) denotes the boundary jet or footprint data of a Wilson hairpin/collar observable approaching the reflection plane.
\(C_\partial\) is the connected coincident-footprint boundary covariance obtained by polarizing the logarithm of the multiplicative anomaly.
The phase \(\alpha(\xi)\) is a diagonal congruence and is same-theory harmless if fixed before the continuum passage.
The logarithmic cross-ratio \(K\) cancels all one-body phases and diagonal factors, isolating the connected pair-dependent boundary term.

equations.label: hairpin anomaly expansion
equations.valid_when: Valid for small smooth hairpin variations when the boundary defect is generated by a positive Gaussian-type second cumulant plus higher connected cumulants.

equations.label: cross-ratio polarization
equations.valid_when: Valid for any nonzero multiplicative anomaly; it is invariant under diagonal congruences and detects the connected pair-dependent boundary term.

equations.label: infinitesimal damping
equations.valid_when: Valid in the second-order regime; it produces the two-by-two normalized damping falsifier for the same-theory OS bridge.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A perturbative or nonperturbative computation giving \(\|\xi-�eta\|_{C_\partial}>0\) for two allowed hairpin boundary jets is a falsifier of the no-boundary-sector same-theory condition. In practice the test is a nonzero \(K\) after diagonal Wilson renormalizations are removed.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This lemma identifies the analytic Yang-Mills estimate needed after the finite-dimensional Schur theorem: prove \(C_\partial=0\) on a dense Wilson core, not merely boundedness of the boundary anomaly.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Infinitesimal hairpin kernel equivalence: on a smooth dense Wilson core, the no-boundary-sector condition is equivalent to vanishing of the connected boundary OPE covariance \(C_\partial\). If small boundary-shape variations \(\xi,\eta\) have anomaly \(B_{\xi\eta}=\exp(i\alpha(\xi)-i\alpha(\eta)-\frac12\|\xi-\eta\|_{C_\partial}^2+o(\|\xi-\eta\|^2))\), then a nonzero \(C_\partial\) gives normalized damping and hence the Schur-rigidity falsifier; \(C_\partial=0\) removes the infinitesimal boundary Hilbert sector up to harmless phases.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot only if an explicit Wilson hairpin computation gives \(|B_{12}|<1\) or \(K\ne0\) in the locked algebra, showing that the RG route proves positivity for an enlarged boundary theory rather than the intended Yang-Mills theory.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote if a dense Wilson-core estimate proves \(C_\partial=0\), or equivalently that every multiplicative boundary anomaly has zero logarithmic cross-ratio and is just a prelocked diagonal congruence.
control_decision.reason: The branch made a real mathematical gain: it replaced the vague multiplicative-anomaly warning with a precise Schur/Gram rigidity lemma and an equivalent no-boundary-sector target. The remaining gap is analytic, not conceptual.

dependency_updates.description: The bridge now has a finite-dimensional necessary condition: after collar positivity gives \(N\ge0\), any multiplicative boundary anomaly \(B\) must have positive reciprocal Schur multiplier. For normalized Gram boundary anomalies this forces rank-one diagonal congruence.

The locked algebra must exclude hidden boundary degrees of freedom. Wilson collar limits are same-theory only if their boundary hairpin state is unique up to phase; otherwise the construction has changed the observable algebra by adjoining \(\mathcal K_\partial\).
The topology must control not only fixed reflected OS forms but also the collar-to-plane limit uniformly enough to identify or rule out the multiplicative anomaly \(B\) and its cross-ratio \(K\).

falsifiers: falsifier: a pair of reflected Wilson hairpin observables with normalized boundary overlap \(|B_{12}|<1\) after all accepted diagonal Wilson renormalizations are removed.
falsifier: a nonzero logarithmic cross-ratio \(K_{12;34}\) for four mixed reflected Wilson collar pairings sharing a coincident boundary footprint.

falsifier: a computed positive boundary covariance \(C_\partial\ne0\) in the infinitesimal hairpin expansion, since it creates a nontrivial boundary Hilbert factor rather than the intended same theory.
falsifier: RG convergence that is valid for separated collars but loses uniformity as the collar thickness approaches the reflection plane, leaving \(B\) undefined or pair-dependent.
falsifier: a proof of reflection positivity only for the enlarged matrix \(N\) while the recovered same-theory matrix \(M=B^{[-1]}\circ N\) fails a two-by-two determinant test.
branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 191 recasts the remaining Wilson obstruction as a boundary Hilbert-sector problem. The formal closed-cone passage is valid for collar matrices, but if collar collapse produces a normalized Gram factor \(B\), then same-theory positivity requires the reciprocal Schur multiplier \(B^{[-1]}\) to be positive. Two-by-two minors plus Cauchy-Schwarz force such a Gram factor to be rank one. Thus the analytic Yang-Mills goal is sharper than generic reflection-positivity preservation: prove that reflected Wilson hairpins have no nontrivial boundary state, equivalently \(K=0\) or \(C_\partial=0\) on the locked Wilson core. Any nonzero boundary covariance is a substantive falsifier, not a removable normalization nuisance.

Express it as a boundary limit of connected curvature insertions; check whether gauge invariance, reflection parity, and bulk renormalization force the resulting \(C_\partial\) to vanish or instead produce a nonzero cusp/hairpin kernel.
